findings.issue_text: [High/api] OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is added as an abstract method to a provider SPI with no default implementation; every existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory (custom grant extensions) will fail to compile/load, and since DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls getShortcut() on every registered grant factory at startup, deployments with custom grants will fail to boot after upgrade (AbstractMethodError). A default method should be provided instead.

[Medium/bug] AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher logic is doubly broken: the condition is inverted (it rejects IDs whose grant matches expectedGrantShortcut) and the grant shortcut lives at chars 5-6 (substring(4, 6)), not substring(3, 5). Net effect: the matcher accepts any grant type, so all the new Details.TOKEN_ID grant assertions are vacuous; fixing only one of the two defects breaks every test using the matcher.

[Medium/bug] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException when the grant type has no registered shortcut, so TokenManager.initToken now hard-fails token issuance (500) whenever the Constants.GRANT_TYPE client-session attribute holds any unregistered value (e.g., set by third-party code via the now-public constant); previously token creation could not fail here. It should degrade to the UNKNOWN/'na' shortcut as it already does for a null attribute.

[Medium/api] The public copy constructor Context(Context) in OAuth2GrantType is deleted, a source/binary incompatible change for any extension code (custom grants) that constructed Contexts this way; no replacement propagation of the new grantType field is offered.

[Medium/api] The shortcut contract is wrong and unvalidated: the javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but the decoder hard-requires exactly 2-char shortcuts (encodedContext.length() != 6 check), and neither postInit nor the lazy refresh validates shortcut length; additionally a factory returning a null shortcut causes an NPE from ConcurrentHashMap.put during postInit (startup failure). A custom grant with a 1- or 3-char shortcut silently produces token IDs that can never be decoded.

[Medium/concurrency] The lazy 'refresh' of the shared maps in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory (getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut) is an unsynchronized check-then-act on provider-singleton state, performs an O(n) factory scan on every persistent miss, and bypasses the startup duplicate-shortcut validation: a lazily added grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites grantsByShortcuts, making previously issued token IDs decode to the wrong grant type. The 'hot deployment' rationale also doesn't match Keycloak's startup-only provider registration.

[Medium/data] The jti of every access token and the Details.TOKEN_ID event detail change format from a plain UUID to xxxyyyzz:uuid for all deployments; any event consumer, log pipeline, test, or client that treats token IDs as UUIDs will break. This intended-but-breaking format change needs explicit documentation/compat handling for consumers.

[Medium/test_gap] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest never calls postInit (it pokes the package-private map fields directly), leaving sessionFactory null; in testIncorrectGrantType the 'ac' lookup misses and the lazy-refresh path NPEs on the null sessionFactory, and since the test catches any RuntimeException it passes for the wrong reason — it never verifies the intended IllegalArgumentException and masks the NPE. The production postInit logic (map population, duplicate-shortcut detection) is untested.

[Medium/test_gap] There are no tests for getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, the primary production path (online/offline/transient session detection, lightweight-vs-regular token detection, grant-type attribute propagation from the actual grant flows); only the string encode/decode round-trip is covered, and the end-to-end event assertions that would cover it are vacuous.

[Low/bug] AccessTokenContext copy-paste defect: Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, 'Null rawTokenId not allowed') checks grantType twice, so rawTokenId is never null-checked despite the message; a null raw ID is accepted and would encode as '...:null'.

[Low/bug] DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId has inconsistent malformed-input handling: IDs without ':' degrade gracefully to UNKNOWN, but IDs with ':' whose context part isn't exactly 6 chars (or contains unknown shortcuts) throw IllegalArgumentException. An attacker-controlled/malformed jti will cause hard failures instead of degrading to UNKNOWN once this is wired to request handling.

[Low/bug] Token creation now transitively depends on session.getContext().getClient() being non-null (via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken), even though initToken already receives the client as a parameter; any path that creates access tokens without a client set in the session context (direct TokenManager use in tooling/tests) will NPE and fail all token issuance where it previously worked.

[Low/security] Encoding session type (online/offline/transient), token type, and grant type into jti discloses this metadata to any recipient of the token (resource servers, logs, proxies) without introspection — e.g., flagging long-lived offline sessions as higher-value targets. This accepted trade-off should be a conscious, documented decision.

goldens.comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (no `default` implementation) in `server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java`. This is a binary-incompatible change for any existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations compiled against the previous interface. The new startup logic in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates `factory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class)` and unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()`, which would trigger an `AbstractMethodError` for such providers and can prevent boot. This behavior is directly shown in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes TokenManager.initToken() always encode the access token ID via TokenContextEncoderProvider (TokenManager.java: initToken now calls encoder.encodeTokenId(...)). DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() only maps a null Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute to UNKNOWN ("na"), but if the attribute is non-null and not present in the factory’s grantType->shortcut map, encodeTokenId() calls factory.getShortcutByGrantType(...) and then throws IllegalStateException when it returns null. This exception is uncaught in initToken, so token issuance can now hard-fail where previously token.id(generateId()) could not fail. The failure condition is verifiable from the new code paths and the strict throw in encodeTokenId().

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java` removes the previously available public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` (lines removed in the hunk) and adds a new `grantType` field initialized only in the primary constructor (`this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);`) plus a getter. This is a source/binary incompatible SPI change for any custom grant/extensions that used the copy constructor to clone/modify a `Context`, and the diff does not provide an alternative copy/clone mechanism that preserves the new `grantType` field. This is an API compatibility concern rather than a direct functional defect in the changed code itself.

The 'hot deployment' rationale also doesn't match Keycloak's startup-only provider registration.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() duplicates are validated only for the initially discovered grant factories by comparing grantsByShortcuts vs grantsToShortcuts sizes. However, both getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() implement a lazy “refresh” on cache miss that does unconditional put()s into the shared ConcurrentHashMap instances without re-checking for shortcut collisions (e.g., grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType)), which would overwrite an existing mapping if a colliding shortcut ever appeared later. The concurrency aspect is mitigated by ConcurrentHashMap (no unsafe mutation), but the check-then-act and collision/overwrite risk on lazy refresh is diff-grounded. Whether ‘hot deployment’ really occurs is not verifiable from the diff, so this is more of an architectural/robustness concern than a definite bug in normal operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] The jti of every access token and the Details.TOKEN_ID event detail change format from a plain UUID to xxxyyyzz:uuid for all deployments; any event consumer, log pipeline, test, or client that treats token IDs as UUIDs will break. adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the access token `jti`/ID from a raw UUID to an encoded format with a context prefix and colon (e.g., `onrtcc:<uuid>`). In `TokenManager.initToken`, `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` is replaced with `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)`, where `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` returns `sessionTypeShortcut + tokenTypeShortcut + grantShortcut + ':' + rawTokenId`. Tests are updated to no longer expect UUIDs for `Details.TOKEN_ID` (e.g., `AssertEvents` now uses `isAccessTokenId(...)`). This is a real, diff-grounded backwards-incompatible format change for token IDs/event details, but it is not inherently a correctness defect in the implementation itself; it’s an API/consumer compatibility concern that likely needs documentation or migration guidance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial production logic in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)` (detect `TRANSIENT` vs `OFFLINE` vs `ONLINE`, `LIGHTWEIGHT` vs `REGULAR` via `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`, and `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` propagation), but the only new unit test (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest`) exercises `getTokenContextFromTokenId(...)` and `encodeTokenId(...)` round-trips, not the client-session-derived path. Additionally, the updated end-to-end event assertions use `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(...)`, whose logic appears inverted/off-by-one (`substring(3,5)` and returning `false` when it equals the expected shortcut), making those assertions ineffective at validating grant-type encoding, supporting the claim that E2E coverage doesn’t meaningfully test the primary path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show inconsistent handling in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId: token IDs without ':' return an AccessTokenContext with UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/na, but token IDs with ':' enforce encodedContext length == 6 and validate shortcuts, throwing IllegalArgumentException on mismatch/unknown values. However, the diff does not show this decoder being used in any request-handling path (only encoding is wired into TokenManager.initToken), so the claim about attacker-controlled/malformed jti causing hard failures in request handling is not directly verifiable from the PR. Still, the robustness concern is real and grounded in the added code.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes access-token ID generation in `TokenManager.initToken(...)` call `encoder.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)`, which in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` calls `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`. That method dereferences `session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...)` with no null-check. `initToken` already receives `ClientModel client` but the new path does not use it, so any invocation where `session.getContext().getClient()` is unset will now NPE during token creation (a new dependency/regression introduced by this change).

This accepted trade-off should be a conscious, documented decision.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes access token jti generation to include encoded context: TokenManager.initToken() now builds an AccessTokenContext and sets token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)). DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId() concatenates sessionType (on/of/tr), tokenType (rt/lt), and a 2-char grant shortcut plus ':' and the raw UUID. This makes session persistence/offline status, token “lightweight” status, and grant type trivially readable by any party that can see the token string (resource servers, logs, proxies) without introspection. That’s a real security/privacy trade-off introduced by this change and should be consciously documented, but it’s not necessarily a correctness bug if intended.
